claims.text: Oxidation resistance and mechanical integrity in high-temperature multiprincipal-element alloys are governed by the kinetics and adherence of a protective oxide scale.
A dense grain-boundary network enhances diffusion of protective-oxide-forming elements such as Cr and Al.
Rapid solidification or laser cladding refines the alloy microstructure and increases grain-boundary density.
Grain refinement accelerates formation of a continuous protective oxide scale.
Trace Y additions promote strong adhesion of the protective oxide scale.
Coarse-grained or unmodified alloys preferentially form non-protective Mn oxides that deplete strengthening elements and degrade integrity.
Conventionally cast CrMnFeCoNi has coarse grains and typically forms discontinuous, non-protective oxide scales at high temperature.
Adding approximately 0.2–0.5 at% Y during laser cladding will produce a nanocrystalline version of the baseline alloy.
Grain-boundary density and nanoscale reactive particles at the oxide/alloy interface mediate formation of a continuous, adherent protective scale.
Grain boundaries act as short-circuit paths for outward diffusion of Cr and Al.
Enhanced Cr and Al diffusion produces stable protective Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scales.
Trace Y forms fine Y2O3 dispersoids at the oxide/alloy interface.
Interfacial Y2O3 particles pin the oxide and improve oxide/alloy bonding, thereby preventing scale spallation.
Y2O3 interfacial pinning reduces stress buildup in the oxide scale.
The combined grain-refinement and Y effects suppress formation of non-protective Mn oxides.
Relative to coarse-grained CrMnFeCoNi, the modified alloy will form a thinner, more continuous, and more adherent protective scale with lower oxidation mass gain.
The modified alloy will exhibit less depletion of strengthening elements and retain higher strength and mechanical integrity after oxidation.
In CrMnFeCoNi, Mn is the principal oxide-forming element during high-temperature oxidation and its non-protective oxides deplete Mn from the bulk.
The proposed behavior should hold for compositionally similar multiprincipal-element alloys at approximately 950–1100 °C when oxidation is diffusion controlled.
The proposed behavior may not apply when liquid-metal embrittlement or irradiation effects dominate degradation.

contradictions.description: The controlled composition is presented as CrMnFeCoNi with only trace Y added, but the mechanism relies partly on Al diffusion and formation of Al2O3 even though no Al is present in the stated baseline or modified composition.

The mechanism proposes protective Cr2O3 formation in the modified CrMnFeCoNi-based comparison, whereas the cited CrMnFeCoNi evidence reports that Cr2O3 was not observed. This is not a direct logical contradiction because processing and Y differ, but the hypothesis does not explain why those changes would reverse the reported oxide selection.
